learning_outcomes.text: The student will learn the importance of Project, as well as its applications to the different fields of engineering, applying the acquired knowledge to the realization of engineering projects.
The student will know the General Theory of Project and will learn the influence of each of its phases in its execution.
Understand and learn to use Project Management as a basis for solving problems that arise in project planning and control.
Learn the characteristics and competencies that any project manager must put into practice, and obtain the necessary skills for project programming and administration during its execution.

syllabus_topics: Concept and function of the Technical Office
The legal framework of the project
Classification and order of precedence of norms
Local, state, and autonomous community regulations
Introduction to the Technical Building Code
Structure of a Regulation. Industrial Regulations
The project as a legal document
Descriptive, constructive, and justificatory report (Specific by specialty)
The material execution of the project
Project assignment. Types of contracts (Specific by specialty)
Proceedings before Official Bodies (Specific by specialty)
Definition of investment costs (Specific by specialty)
Economic and financial studies of the project
Criteria for project evaluation and selection
Planning, scheduling, and control techniques (Specific by specialty)
BASIC REGULATIONS APPLICABLE TO THE INDUSTRIAL PROJECT
Application of building and construction regulations to the project (Specific by specialty)
Application of electrical installation regulations to the project
Application of telecommunications installation regulations to the project
COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN PROJECT ENGINEERING I
Analysis, debugging, and optimization of results
Generation of project documentation using software
COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN PROJECT ENGINEERING II
Generation of project documentation using BIM
teaching_methods: Seminar or problem-solving activities in class

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical/practical final exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: A minimum score of 5 points is required in both the theoretical and practical components to average them. If any component scores less than 5 points, no compensation is applied. In this case, the final grade will be the arithmetic mean if it is below 4.50; otherwise, the final grade will be capped at 4.50 points. The theoretical exam consists of two parts, each requiring a minimum of 5 points to pass, and passed parts are carried over to resits.
